summary: Skamania Co., WA: 1938 L-4 cab, DNR cabs in 1955 and 1973/74, last cab removed 1982; WTA describes a hike to a flattened summit.

facts.design: 2-story L-4 cab (1938), then 14-by-14-foot DNR ground cabs (1955 and 1973 or 1974)
facts.status_note: The last cab was sold and removed in 1982. WTA describes a flattened summit where a lookout formerly stood, with concrete steps below it.

staffing.status: Kit Carson McCoy named for 1948 in a 1990s interview; Kay Love listed as lookout personnel in 1951

access.note: WTA describes a hike that starts from the Pacific Crest Trail. No source read reports a closure.

visit.trail_note: WTA's shorter route is 4.2 miles round trip with about 1,200 feet of gain, starting where the Pacific Crest Trail crosses Road CG 2090.

events.note: Panoramic photos from the summit show a viewing post and a living cabin below.
2-story L-4 cab, the first structure on the summit, likely developed by the Columbia National Forest.
In February 1942 the Forest Service told the state it was abandoning the lookout house; the state said it would rehabilitate it.
Kit Carson McCoy, per Gene Sargent's 1990s interview.
Kay Love listed as lookout personnel.
State 14-by-14-foot ground cabin of plywood and glass.
The Oregonian reported the lookout was to be discontinued because of air patrols and would most likely be burned. WillhiteWeb says the burning apparently did not happen.
Second identical DNR cab: 1973 per the register and Firelookout.com; 1974 per a 1974 annual report quoted by the Washington lookouts site and WillhiteWeb.
Cab sold and removed by a private party. WillhiteWeb says Dick Morrison placed it on his house in Friday Harbor.
Registered in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on July 18, 2012.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com date the second identical DNR cab to 1973. The Washington lookouts site quotes a 1974 annual report, and WillhiteWeb also dates the new cab to 1974. The sources do not reconcile the years.
Only WillhiteWeb says where the cab went (a house in Friday Harbor). The register and Firelookout.com say only that it was sold and removed in 1982.

notes_for_editor: The Friday Harbor location rests on one page and is not verified. The 1973 versus 1974 year conflict is left open. Today's description comes from a current WTA hiking page; WillhiteWeb photo captions (footings, a site photo labeled current location) are undated. Brief status, agency and elevation check out; no corrections.
